newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heating oil ends off as supply build seen.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heating oil ends off as supply build seen.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil ended lower Tuesday amid expectations that oil inventory data would show increased supply just as some weather forecastes were calling for more moderate-than-expected weather in the U.S. Northeast.

"Some of the decline was an expectation of a stock build while part of it was a recognition that yesterday's rally was overdone since some forecasts indicated the cold weather won't persist," said Dean Witter analyst Steve Platt.
February heating oil settled 1.15 cents a gallon lower at 72.49 cents.
Crude and gasoline were caught in heating oil's downdraft, with February crude finishing off 14 cents at $26.23 a barrel and February gasoline ending off 0.42 cent at 72.10 cents a gallon.

"Crude suffered just a small dip, but the uptrend is still intact," said a crude dealer in Cleveland. Many dealers expected prompt crude near-term to test the $26.80 post-Gulf War high crude hit December 19.
Prompt crude remains above its simple 20-day moving average while the 14-day Relative Strength Indicator was a neutral 59.

Tuesday evening the American Petroleum Institute (API) reported that for the week ended January 3 distillate stocks grew 2.94 million barrels, surpassing trader expectations of a build around 1.5 million barrels.
Distillate stocks are comprised of heating oil and diesel.
Dealers expected unseasonably mild weather last week to have cut demand while seasonal inventory trends pointed to a build anyway.

Meanwhile, after several private forecasters had said Monday that temperatures would be below normal in the key heating oil market of the northeastern United States this week, Weather Services Corp's six-to-10 day forecast Tuesday called for near normal temperatures in the region, which would temper heating oil demand.
The most recent National Weather Service's six-to-10 day forecast concurred with Weather Services.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
